1. (Currently Amended) A lamp comprised of an at least substantially hollow columnar body, a plurality of light emitting diodes disposed on said columnar body, a plurality of fins disposed on said columnar body, a base member disposed at a first end of the columnar body and providing a means for electrical connection, an electronics module disposed within the columnar body and in electrical communication with the base member, wherein said light emitting diodes are mounted on said columnar body using a surface-mount assembly process, and wherein said electronics module comprises a printed circuit board with circuitry for converting AC to DC current and controlling brightness of said light emitting diodes.

2. (Currently Amended) The lamp of claim 1 wherein a second end of said columnar body is open and said open end is configured to permit thermal convection.

3. (Currently Amended) The lamp of claim 1 further including a light dispersing optic element overlapping said diodes, wherein said optic element is integrally formed with said columnar body or separately attached thereto.

4. (Currently Amended) The lamp of claim 3 wherein said optic element includes a phosphor material and is configured to convert at least a portion of light from said diodes to a different wavelength.

5. (Original) The lamp of claim 1 wherein said diodes are substantially evenly spaced radially around the columnar body.

6. (Currently Amended) The lamp of claim 5 wherein said fins are substantially equally disposed between said diodes and said fins are configured to provide both thermal dissipation and light transmission surfaces.

7. (Original) The lamp of claim 1 wherein said columnar body comprises one of a tetragon, pentagon, hexagon, heptagon, octagon, nonagon, decagon, hendecagon, or dodecagon in cross-section.

8. (Original) The lamp of claim 7 wherein at least one diode resides on each face of said columnar body.

9. (Original) The lamp of claim 8 wherein one fin resides on each corner of said columnar body.

10. (Currently Amended) The lamp of claim 9 wherein a single diode resides on each face and said single diode on each face is positioned at the center of each face.

11. (Original) The lamp of claim 1 wherein said columnar body and said fins are comprised of a material having a thermal conductivity greater than 100 W/mK.

12. (Currently Amended) The lamp of claim 9 wherein a single optic element is disposed between each adjacent fin overlapping said diode, and said optic element is configured to collimate light from said diode in a direction perpendicular to said columnar body axis.

13. (Original) The lamp of claim 1 wherein said base member comprises an Edison screw base or a wedge base.

14. (Currently Amended) The lamp of claim 1 wherein said electronics module comprises a printed circuit board including circuitry for converting AC to DC current and further including a dimming control circuit for adjusting brightness of said light emitting diodes.

15. (Currently Amended) The lamp of claim 3 wherein said optic element preferentially directs light substantially perpendicular to an elongated axis of the columnar body and said optic element has a refractive index greater than 1.5.

16. (Currently Amended) A lamp comprising an elongated hollow polygonal body comprised of a material having a thermal conductivity greater than 100 W/mK, a fin extending radially from each corner of said body, a light emitting diode mounted to each side of said body using surface-mount technology, a screw or wedge base connector closing a first end of said body, a second end of said body being open to permit thermal convection, an electronics module disposed within said body in electrical communication with said connector and said light emitting diodes, said electronics module including a printed circuit board with AC to DC conversion circuitry and brightness control circuitry, said lamp having a general A19 outline, and wherein said light emitting diodes are controlled to operate at a specific color temperature.

17. (Currently Amended) A method of manufacturing a lamp comprising extruding an elongated hollow body, said body comprised of a material having a thermal conductivity greater than 100 W/mK, cutting said body to a predetermined length, surface-mounting at least one light emitting diode to said body using solder reflow or adhesive bonding, and providing electrical circuitry suitable for powering said light emitting diode, wherein said circuitry includes AC to DC conversion and brightness control functionality.

18. (Original) The method of claim 17 wherein said material has a thermal conductivity greater than about 150 W/mK.

19. (Original) The method of claim 17 wherein said body includes a plurality of integral radially extending fins.

20. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 17 wherein said body has substantially straight side walls and said side walls are formed during the extrusion process.
